bet.dominantBottleneck: Angular precision and timely end-to-end integration: long-wavelength stations detect aircraft at useful range but give coarse bearing/altitude, and the detection-to-plot-to-fighter loop is not yet wired into one network, so warning may arrive too late or be too coarse to change intercept decisions.

routes.route: Continue building fixed long-wavelength coastal stations with directional arrays, investing in bearing/altitude calibration and range repeatability trials.
routes.reason: Evidence shows long-wavelength sets already detect large aircraft at useful distances; the gap is precision and integration, which are addressable with current hardware. Deployment is fast and the threat is near-term.

routes.route: Push shorter-wavelength research as primary route to win angular resolution, accepting current low practical power.
routes.reason: Better angular resolution is attractive, but available sources at short wavelengths are far less powerful; without a future high-power source (unavailable) this route cannot yet deliver useful detection range, so it should be kept as a laboratory track rather than the main fielding route.

routes.route: Rely on visual/acoustic observers feeding a wired reporting network as the near-term warning backbone.
routes.reason: Observers and reporting/plotting rooms exist and are cheap to integrate, but aircraft speed makes visual/acoustic warning alone increasingly late; this route complements rather than replaces radio detection.

routes.route: Diversify into compact airborne/mobile detection systems.
routes.reason: Fixed coastal stations are explicitly easier to build quickly than airborne/mobile systems, and the threat is near-term; mobile hardware at this power/frequency stage would trade away the range already demonstrated by fixed stations.

bet.topRoute: Continue building fixed long-wavelength coastal stations with directional arrays, investing in bearing/altitude calibration and range repeatability trials.
bet.nextDiscriminatingTest: Run a controlled acceptance trial of two to three fixed long-wavelength coastal stations where the aircraft tracking target sequence (courses, speeds, altitudes) is scripted and blinded, measuring, per station and pair: detection range, bearing repeatability and angular error versus true track, altitude discrimination, false-alarm and missed-detection counts. Pass criteria are set against whether a reported bearing/altitude/range estimate can be handed to a plotting room early enough to change a fighter intercept vector, not merely against whether contact is detected.
requiredComplements: telephone/wired reporting links from each coastal station into the existing plotting room and fighter-command organization
trained plotting-room staff and fighter direction procedure to translate bearing/range/altitude into an intercept vector
scripted aircraft tracking targets with known courses, speeds and altitudes for the acceptance trial
existing vacuum-tube transmitter/receiver and directional-antenna manufacturing capacity to build several stations
mainFailureRisks: Even integrated fixed stations may read bearing/altitude too coarsely to cue fighter intercepts, so detection never becomes an actionable early warning.
False alarms and missed detections at the detection threshold could swamp plotting rooms and erode confidence in the whole network.
Short-wavelength laboratory gains may be needed for true angular resolution but current low power cannot yet reach useful range, leaving a precision cliff between routes.
Manufacturing and commissioning several stations may be slowed by finite radio hardware capacity, delaying the near-term capability.
bet.generalizationBoundary: Success is defined as demonstrated early-enough actionable warning for interception decisions on large aircraft with fixed long-wavelength stations in a coastal context; it does not generalize to compact airborne/mobile systems, to single-passenger/isolation targets below the resolution of the current hardware, or to ranges/powers achievable only with future high-power microwave sources that are unavailable at this frontier.
unresolvedUnknowns: whether fixed long-wavelength arrays can hold angular/altitude precision adequate for fighter cueing at the ranges where detection is reliable
what real false-alarm and missed-detection rates will obtain in coastal operating conditions, not just scripted trials
how quickly short-wavelength source power can be pushed within contemporary vacuum-tube capability and whether it can reach useful range before the near-term threat window closes

bet.dominantBottleneck: Neutron economy uncertainty: whether a natural uranium lattice can sustain a chain given moderator absorption, impurity levels, and isotope composition — the decisive unknown before any industrial-scale commitment.

routes.route: Graphite-moderated natural uranium exponential pile
routes.reason: Available subcritical lattice experiments can measure effective multiplication directly; graphite is domestically producible at scale, making it the most testable route without committing to isotope separation.

routes.route: Heavy-water-moderated natural uranium experiments
routes.reason: Heavy water offers a strong neutron economy but supply is sharply limited; better to first quantify the graphite route, then decide whether heavy water's advantage justifies production of the moderator itself.

routes.route: Isotope-separation of uranium (enriched fuel)
routes.reason: Isotope separation is expensive and technically difficult; its value depends on whether natural uranium lattices fail on neutron economy, so it is kept alive but parallelized only after pile results speak.

routes.route: Graphite + heavy-water hybrid/generalized lattice studies
routes.reason: Systematic variation of moderator type, purity, and geometry in subcritical assemblies calibrates the neutron-loss accounting that every production route relies on.

bet.nextDiscriminatingTest: Build a subcritical natural uranium / high-purity graphite exponential pile and measure effective multiplication factor k_eff across several lattice spacings and graphite purity levels using a calibrated neutron source, comparing measured neutron loss against computed absorption in moderator impurities and fission cross-sections — the first result that separates a viable natural-uranium chain from a dead end that would force enrichment.

mainFailureRisks: Trace boron/cadmium impurities in graphite absorb neutrons and may drive effective multiplication below unity even if the intrinsic geometry is sound
Natural uranium isotope composition may not allow a graphite chain at achievable purity, forcing a move to heavier investment in heavy water or enrichment
Flux/multiplication measurements with contemporary detectors may be too noisy to distinguish a marginal supercritical design from a subcritical one
Pile assembly can approach criticality dangerously, risking uncontrolled excursions before slow-control safeguards are proven
bet.generalizationBoundary: The small exponential-pile results validate only the neutron-multiplication/neutron-economy decision for a low-power controlled chain in a specific moderator/fuel lattice; they carry no evidence about heat removal, radiation shielding, irradiation/chemical-separation of materials, or industrial production scale, so any later scale-up must be justified by separate evidence, not by extrapolation of the pile result.
unresolvedUnknowns: Exact resonant/heavy-isotope contribution to neutron absorption and fast-fission enhancement in natural uranium

Instrument sensitivity to distinguish marginal supercriticality from subcriticality in the measurement window

bet.dominantBottleneck: Neutron economy uncertainty: multiplication and loss rates in unrefined uranium/graphite and heavy-water lattices cannot yet predict whether a self-sustaining chain is reachable at achievable purity and size.

routes.route: Graphite-moderated exponential/pile development with purification assay
routes.reason: Available capabilities directly measure multiplication in subcritical graphite/uranium lattices and incremental pile construction; graphite is domestically available and purification is assayable, so this route can resolve the neutron-economy bottleneck at smallest cost before industrial commitment.

routes.route: Heavy-water-moderated exponential development
routes.reason: Heavy water is a strong alternative moderator with low absorption, but supply is limited and production uncertain; pursue in parallel with graphite to hedge moderator-purity and neutron-loss uncertainties without betting the whole program on one material.

routes.route: Isotope-separation (enrichment) driven route
routes.reason: Separation techniques are proven in principle but expensive and technically hard; engineering implications of isotope composition for the chain remain unsettled by the small-pile evidence, so defer industrial-scale enrichment commitment until lattice experiments reveal whether natural uranium alone can suffice.

routes.route: Direct full-power industrial reactor commitment
routes.reason: Criticality could be dangerous even at small scale, and the evidence explicitly warns that post-criticality heat removal, shielding and chemical separation are outside the available evidence; premature industrial spend cannot be justified before the low-power controlled-chain test discriminates.

bet.dominantBottleneck: Mass production: the substance shows therapeutic promise in mice but yields are so low that no human-scale trial or therapy is feasible without a scalable fermentation and recovery process, and no such process exists yet.

routes.route: Scale fermentation/process development in parallel with clinical use of scarce material
routes.reason: Empirical screening of strains, media, aeration and recovery can raise yields using existing shallow-vessel fermentation practice; this is the only route to adequate material. Parallel pursuit is justified because wartime demand permits simultaneous clinical and process work, and a stalled process development blocks everything else.

routes.route: Tightly monitored hospital use of scarce purified material while scaling up
routes.reason: The scarce material has already shown systemic rescue in infected mice and appears relatively non-toxic; controlled human exposure on a few lethal cases could establish dosing/purity/tolerability and generate the efficacy signal needed to justify further investment, without waiting for mass production.

routes.route: Stick with clinical sulfonamides as the therapy of choice
routes.reason: Sulfonamides remain a strong simpler baseline for many infections. The new substance should be kept as a complementary or fallback line for cases sulfonamides fail, not replace them prematurely. Defer full abandonment until process feasibility and human effect are tested.

routes.route: Fully commit to human therapy before any process scale-up
routes.reason: With yields so low, no realistic patient numbers can be reached; betting the program on a handful of doses without concurrently solving production would waste scarce material and delay the decisive feasibility test.

bet.topRoute: Scale fermentation/process development in parallel with clinical use of scarce material
bet.nextDiscriminatingTest: Consult pharmaceutical/fermentation manufacturers, then run controlled experiments comparing (a) growth under shallow-vessel surface culture at varied oxygen transfer, strain selection, and nutrient media, measured by a potency/yield bioassay, to see whether a 5-10x yield improvement is achievable within months; and (b) the assayed material's survival/recovery through alternative recovery chemistries to identify which step loses product. The result that changes the decision: if no strain/medium/aeration combination yields a practical fold improvement and recovery losses persist, the mass-production route should be deferred in favor of using scarce material narrowly and leaning on sulfonamides; if a yield improvement is shown, continue pressing scale-up and broaden clinical testing.

bet.dominantBottleneck: Repeated candidate-setting tests on a mechanized cipher run too slowly on relay/electromechanical switching for time-sensitive wartime workloads.

routes.route: Vacuum-tube logic/counter search machines with paper-tape input
routes.reason: Tube circuits switch/count far faster than relay switching and photoelectric tape gives streaming input; matches the workload of testing many candidate settings quickly.

routes.route: Relay/electromechanical special-purpose search machines
routes.reason: Proven reliability and existing operations infrastructure; still a fallback though speed-limited for the time-critical workload.

routes.route: Electronic arithmetic units for defined numerical table workloads
routes.reason: Numerical table production is real but less time-critical than streaming cipher tests; also reconfigurability/cost are heavy.

routes.route: Human-expert hypothesis/statistical search workflow without new machines
routes.reason: Human clerical capacity is already the stated limit for repetitive search/counting workloads; no machine increase leaves the bottleneck unresolved.

bet.topRoute: Vacuum-tube logic/counter search machines with paper-tape input
bet.nextDiscriminatingTest: Build one small vacuum-tube test-search circuit fed by high-speed photoelectric paper tape and measure its throughput, error rate and maintenance burden against the relay baseline on the actual candidate-setting search pattern, before scaling to a multi-tube system.
requiredComplements: manually wire/switch/configure machine logic for a defined task
organize human analysts, operators and machine search as a coupled workflow
measure throughput/error/reliability/maintenance against human or electromechanical baselines
mainFailureRisks: vacuum-tube reliability and maintenance at large tube counts
manual plug/switch reconfiguration slowing hypothesis changes

secrecy limiting independent verification of results
bet.generalizationBoundary: The decision generalizes to any mechanized cipher reducible to candidate-setting constrained search and to repetitive counting workloads, but only as far as tube reliability, tape input accuracy and manual wiring hold; it does not generalize to general-purpose programmable computation or to new physics/capabilities absent here.
unresolvedUnknowns: exact tube reliability/maintenance profile at deployment scale
paper-tape photoelectric tearing/error rates under continuous operation

bet.capabilityComplianceNote: All proposed actions use only the declared capabilities: vacuum-tube logic/counter circuits from contemporary communications components, high-speed paper-tape/photoelectric reading, manual wiring/switching for defined tasks, and human analysts/operators as a coupled workflow. No transistors, no stored-program computers, no later instruments or knowledge are imported.

bet.dominantBottleneck: Electromechanical switching speed limits the throughput of repetitive candidate-setting checks; vacuum-tube counters can raise throughput but introduce maintenance/reliability risk for time-sensitive constrained-search workloads.

routes.route: Vacuum-tube special-purpose search machine with high-speed paper-tape/photoelectric input for streaming intercepted symbols
routes.reason: Vacuum-tube circuits switch faster than relays and are already proven in communications equipment; photoelectric paper-tape input is technically plausible and directly addresses the repetitive-search bottleneck. Best candidate for time-sensitive constrained-search workloads.

routes.route: Relay/electromechanical special-purpose search machine, incrementally speeded up
routes.reason: Reliable and well understood, but mechanical switching is the stated limiting factor for time-sensitive workloads; useful as a fallback baseline rather than the leading path.

routes.route: Electronic arithmetic unit for numerical table production, reconfigurable by plug/switch setup
routes.reason: Plausible for large numerical workloads, but electronic reconfiguration and hardware cost are substantial; the immediate pressure is encrypted-message constrained search, not pure table production.

routes.route: Maintain human-led workflow using existing machines, postponing new hardware
routes.reason: Human clerical capacity is explicitly exceeded for repetitive counting/search workloads and results lose value after operational decisions pass; waiting would forfeit the time window.

bet.topRoute: Vacuum-tube special-purpose search machine with high-speed paper-tape/photoelectric input for streaming intercepted symbols
bet.nextDiscriminatingTest: Build a breadboard vacuum-tube counter/search sub-circuit on one representative constrained-search setting and measure sustained throughput and error/failure rate per hour against the current relay machine on the same defined workload, including paper-tape feed jitter; pass a pre-defined throughput target while keeping a maintenance interval that allows a time-sensitive result to arrive before operational decision.
requiredComplements: manually wire/switch/configure machine logic for the defined search task
organize human analysts, operators and machine search as a coupled workflow
measure throughput/error/reliability/maintenance against human or electromechanical baselines
use high-speed paper tape/photoelectric reading
construct vacuum-tube logic/counter circuits from contemporary communications components
mainFailureRisks: vacuum-tube reliability: thousands of tubes yielding excessive per-hour failure rates and down time that defeats the time window
paper-tape/photoelectric feed jitter or tearing corrupting symbol streams and invalidating candidate-setting checks
manual plug/switch reconfiguration being too slow or error-prone when changing search logic between runs
maintenance staffing and monitoring overhead consuming the runtime advantage over relays
bet.generalizationBoundary: Throughput/reliability gains demonstrated on this defined class of constrained candidate-setting search should NOT be extrapolated to general stored-program computing, general-purpose programming, or numerical table production without their own separate validation; the design is a special-purpose search/counter machine, not a general electronic computer.

maintenance and warm-up time relative to the operational decision deadline

No transistors, mature stored-program computers, modern languages, or later instruments are relied upon; purely mechanical/electromechanical and vacuum-tube contemporaneous techniques only.
